rules.explanation: Writing implementation code before tests often leads to untestable architecture, tight coupling, and missed edge cases.
rules.do: Practice Test-Driven Development: write a failing automated test first (Red), write the minimum production code to pass it (Green), and then refactor safely.
rules.dont: Do not write complex production codebases without accompanying automated test suites.

rules.rule_name: Comprehensive Unit Testing and Mocking Isolations
rules.explanation: Coupling unit tests directly to external databases, live network APIs, or file systems makes tests slow, flaky, and unreliable.
rules.do: Isolate unit tests using mocks, stubs, and fakes to test individual components and business logic functions independently.
rules.dont: Do not make actual network requests or write to live production databases inside standard unit test suites.

rules.explanation: Verifying individual functions in isolation does not guarantee that different modules, services, or databases will integrate correctly together.
rules.do: Implement integration and E2E tests to validate cross-module communication, database transactions, and critical user interaction flows.
rules.dont: Do not rely exclusively on unit tests while neglecting full system integration points.

rules.rule_name: High Test Code Coverage and Quality Metrics
rules.explanation: Releasing code with low test coverage metrics leaves critical code branches vulnerable to undetected edge-case bugs.
rules.do: Monitor and maintain high code test coverage thresholds (e.g., aiming for 80%+ line and branch coverage) within CI/CD quality gates.
rules.dont: Do not merge code changes that introduce untested business logic paths or degrade overall repository test coverage.
